title: Mackenzie overland to the Pacific, 1793
summary: Mackenzie left Fort Fork on the Peace River on 9 May 1793 with six voyageurs, two Indigenous hunters and a dog. He went up the Peace, over the Continental Divide, and down the Parsnip and the Fraser, then left the Fraser on the advice of the people he met and took the Indigenous trading trail over the mountains to the Bella Coola River. He reached the Pacific at Bella Coola on 20 July, and on 22 July wrote his name on a rock in Dean Channel.

events.label: The Pacific at Dean Channel
events.text: He mixed vermilion and bear grease and wrote on a rock: Alex Mackenzie, from Canada, by land, 22nd July 1793. The Heiltsuk, who lived there, were not friendly, and he left soon.
